symptom: mendixlabs/mxcli#1421: `describe module ... with all` omits whole document types (nanoflows, snippets, JS actions, JSON structures, import/export mappings, task queues, image collections) with no error; on PedApp it emitted 0 of FeedbackModule's 11 nanoflows and 20 of its 49 documents.
cause: describeModule's WITH ALL branch was a hand-written section per document type covering 13 types while describe handlers exist for 30-odd; every section was `if err == nil { ... }`, so a failing list or describe was skipped too.
fix: One ordered registry (moduleDocKindsBefore/AfterDomainModel) of describable document kinds, each rendered through describeByKind (the dispatch extracted from execDescribe); a type-blind ListDocumentUnits pass prints `-- not describable: <kind> M.N` for any module unit no entry emitted; read-only reports (building block, icon collection) are emitted commented out; a describe or list failure prints `-- describe failed: ...` and fails the statement after the rest is written (as #1425 does).
test: TestDescribeModuleWithAll_AccountsForEveryDocument (each unit's own describe must appear in the dump; reverted: FeedbackModule 20 of 49, Atlas_Web_Content 0 of 88), TestModuleDocKindsCoverDescribableTypes, TestDescribeModuleWithAll_ReportsDescribeFailure
insight: **A per-type list next to a type-blind enumeration is the drift signal** — this was the fourth hand-kept copy of 'which document types exist' (catalog view, describe_auto, cmd/mxcli dispatch, scriptdiff). Count against ListDocumentUnits, which cannot miss a kind because it never asks for one, and compare each document's own describe output rather than counting `create` lines: a count passes when a document is dumped under the wrong name.
